mbm-1051.clue: That robot owes me a thimble.
mbm-1051.quote: I needed a curved roof for the service station under my mecha. An old red thimble fit perfectly. My mother recognized it from across the room and asked how much they charge for repairs.

mbm-1052.clue: I send my regards to the blue bakery.
mbm-1052.quote: I strung a little radio antenna above our apartment window. On my first call the woman answering described the striped awning of the blue bakery across the way. We’d waved at each other for years without hearing each other’s voices.

mbm-1053.clue: I made a desk clock that sulks.
mbm-1053.quote: My clock program shows a tiny moon asleep until I press the space bar. I added little slippers for its first steps. Some mornings I tap the key a second time just to see the moon stumble.

mbm-1054.quote: I keep the brass tag from the first locker I rented as a kid. It rings against my goggles as I walk to the early swim. The lifeguard calls me the breakfast bell.

mbm-1055.clue: I built a robot a place to sit.
mbm-1055.quote: After a week of painting my mecha I made a little bus shelter from a tea carton. I perched it there with a tiny shopping bag. Even giant machines deserve a ride home.

mbm-1056.clue: I looked down for a whole afternoon.
mbm-1056.quote: Our walking tour followed brass stars set into the pavement. Beside the harbor one star had a crab shell on it. I drew the shell in my guidebook and missed the big statue completely.

mbm-1057.clue: I knit the ending into my slippers.
mbm-1057.quote: I keep a spool of yarn beside the sofa. When our weekly mystery ends, I stitch one tiny colored loop into my slipper cuff. The red loops are the weeks I guessed the culprit.

mbm-1058.clue: I do my warmups with the window open.
mbm-1058.quote: An old fellow across the courtyard answers my last sung note on his trumpet. We’ve never picked a key ahead of time. Our neighbors can tell whose turn it is with the window open.

mbm-1059.clue: I mark my sets with a clothes peg.
mbm-1059.quote: I move a wooden peg along the spokes of the old gym clock between weight sets. My training partner painted one end orange so I can read my count from the mat.

mbm-1060.clue: I use the lake as tracing paper.
mbm-1060.quote: From the middle of my canoe I drew the boathouse roof and its reflection as one diamond. A fish broke the lower corner. I left that ripple right in the drawing.

mbm-1061.clue: I paddled into a room without a roof.
mbm-1061.quote: The reeds opened into a little circle just wide enough for my kayak. I rested the paddle across my lap and listened to every rustle outside the green walls.

mbm-1062.clue: I draw the shoes before the heroes.
mbm-1062.quote: At anime club we stopped a chase scene and made up owners for all the abandoned shoes outside a door. My favorite was a battered purple slipper belonging to a retired space pilot.

mbm-1063.clue: I used the last blue on the shadow.
mbm-1063.quote: I painted a yellow house all afternoon. Just before packing up I noticed the blue shadow beneath the steps. That last brushstroke made the house look cool enough to step into.

mbm-1064.clue: I know which flower goes by the hem.
mbm-1064.quote: I embroidered a red hibiscus low on the skirt of my aunt’s pollera so my smallest cousin could reach it. The first time she twirled, he followed his flower around the courtyard.

mbm-1065.clue: I follow the bridges with red rails.
mbm-1065.quote: My cycling map got wet, leaving only a row of red bridges along the canal. I rode from rail to rail and found a little orchard at the last one. I carry that blurred map on purpose now.

mbm-1066.clue: I look for the stamp under the saucer.
mbm-1066.quote: I bought mismatched saucers at a market because each had a different blue mark underneath. On Sundays we turn them over after tea and invent a country for each little crown and bird.

mbm-1067.quote: On my first tandem jump the canopy opened above us and the rushing noise fell away. I could hear the instructor grinning before I turned my head. That quiet is the part I keep trying to describe.

mbm-1068.clue: I carry a blue ribbon in my canoe bag.
mbm-1068.quote: A gust blew my friend’s ribbon into a branch over the creek. I steadied the canoe while she reached up for it. We tied it to the handle afterward and let the breeze have another go.

mbm-1069.clue: I keep the stone with the tiny chip.
mbm-1069.quote: When I was learning baduk I tapped my grandfather’s board too hard and chipped a white stone. He lets me use that stone for the first move of each lesson. My hand has gotten gentler.

mbm-1070.clue: I’m writing a map with a missing street.
mbm-1070.quote: I spilled tea on my notebook and one corner of my fictional town vanished. Now my characters can’t remember where that street went either. The postman has a bag full of undeliverable clues.

mbm-1071.quote: On the radio one evening I caught a lookout reporting birds on a distant cliff. His pencil broke mid-count. I kept tally beside my receiver and read the number back to him.

mbm-1072.clue: I like the end of the platform after rain.
mbm-1072.quote: Steam from the old engine hangs over the puddles for a few seconds. I sketched the engine upside down in one puddle while my friend kept watch for the station cat.

mbm-1073.clue: My aunt’s laundry basket runs a strong defense.
mbm-1073.quote: We play flying-disc golf across her yard with the basket as the last hole. One gust carried a bedsheet right over the goal. We had to wait out a very patient goalkeeper.

mbm-1074.clue: I made my uncle a loop for a pencil.
mbm-1074.quote: My uncle repairs clocks and loses pencils. I cut him a narrow leather loop with a brass snap. When I visited he had put a daisy in it and lost the pencil again.

mbm-1075.clue: I can find my ball by touch.
mbm-1075.quote: I put a tiny felt bow on the zipper of my bowling bag. At our dim little alley I can pick it out with my eyes shut. My cousin thinks I should try the same trick on the lane.
